title: Joan of Arc
objective: After this level you can explain Joan of Arc's rise, trial and legacy.
summary: Joan of Arc helped lift the siege of Orléans and saw Charles VII crowned in 1429. Captured in 1430, she was tried at Rouen, burned in 1431, cleared in 1456 and made a saint in 1920.

cards.headline: A farmer’s daughter turned the war around. Then a court set a trap for her.
cards.body: We know what Joan of Arc said at her trial, because the record survives. First, how she got there.

cards.headline: Voices and a siege
cards.body: Joan was born about 1412, the daughter of a tenant farmer at Domrémy in eastern France. She believed the voices of St Michael, St Catherine and St Margaret were telling her to help the dauphin Charles and drive out the English. In May 1429 she helped lift the English siege of Orléans. On 17 July Charles was crowned at Reims, with Joan near the altar holding her banner. From a siege to a coronation in about ten weeks.

cards.headline: Captured and tried
cards.body: In 1430 Burgundian troops, allies of the English, captured her at Compiègne and handed her over to the English. From January 1431 a church court at Rouen, led by Pierre Cauchon, Bishop of Beauvais, put her on trial. Its record is unusually full for a medieval trial, so we can still read the judges’ questions and her answers.

cards.headline: The trick question
cards.body: The judges asked whether she knew she was in God’s grace. It was a trap: the Church held that no one could know. Say yes, and she sounded like a heretic; say no, and she admitted guilt. On 24 February 1431 Joan answered: “If I am not, may God place me there; if I am, may God so keep me.” Neither yes nor no, and nothing to catch.

mascot.line: No yes, no no, and no way to catch her. The record kept her exact words.

cards.headline: Condemned, then cleared
cards.body: The court condemned her anyway. After recanting in May, she was found wearing men’s clothes again and declared a relapsed heretic. On 30 May 1431 she was burned at the stake in Rouen, aged about 19. In 1455–56 a retrial authorised by Pope Callixtus III annulled her sentence, and in 1920 she was made a saint.

questions.prompt: What did Joan of Arc help to do at Orléans in May 1429?

options.label: Crown Charles VII
options.rationale: That happened at Reims in July.

options.label: Sign a peace treaty with England
Lift the English siege of the city

questions.explanation: In May 1429 Joan helped lift the English siege of Orléans.

questions.prompt: At her 1431 trial, why was asking Joan if she was in God’s grace a trap?

options.label: She had never heard of God’s grace before her trial
The Church held no one could know, so yes or no hurt her
Any answer she gave would be kept secret from the court
Only a bishop was allowed to answer that question
options.rationale: The trap was in the doctrine.

questions.explanation: Church teaching held that no one could be sure: yes sounded like heresy, no like admitting guilt.

questions.prompt: Joan fought for Charles VII’s right to the French crown. Whose rival claim had started the Hundred Years’ War?

options.label: The Duke of Burgundy’s
options.rationale: Burgundy fought alongside England; the claim was Edward’s.

questions.explanation: Edward III claimed the French crown through his mother, Isabella, in 1328.
